  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

I**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

d**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.

- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

y**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

g**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

n**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

w**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally

- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

 **The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

s**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally

- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

h**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

c**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

itself in YouTube Studio.

itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

o**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

n**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

T**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.

- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

o**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

m**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"
```

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.
- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.
- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

- Both empty leaves a branded placeholder frame with a "Film — placeholder" badge.

  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.

**On captions:** `cc_load_policy=0` means "don't force captions on", and that is as far as the
YouTube player API goes. There is no parameter that forces captions *off* — a viewer whose own
YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

YouTube account prefers captions will still see them, and nothing in this page can override
that. To guarantee no captions for anyone, remove or unpublish the caption track on the video
itself in YouTube Studio.

2**The video** is set on the `#videoFrame` element in the markup, not in the config block.
It currently points at the YouTube film:

```
data-embed="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/got4YYzsbYg?autoplay=1&rel=0&cc_load_policy=0&modestbranding=1"

- Self-hosted instead: clear `data-embed` and set `data-src="media/film.mp4"`, optionally
  `data-poster="media/poster.jpg"`.

- Nothing is embedded until the visitor clicks play, so no YouTube request — and no YouTube
  cookie — happens on page view. `youtube-nocookie.com` keeps it that way after play too.
